record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: For personalized federated learning, how can model architectures incorporate user and context features, how should multi-task or clustered-client algorithms choose the number and grouping of models, and under what conditions is a shared global federated model better than independent per-client models or personalized local fine-tuning?

evidence.quote: when is a global model better?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning setup with $N$ clients, where client $i$ has a local data distribution $\mathcal{D}_i$ over an input-output space $\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$ and a (possibly client-specific) loss function $\ell_i$. Three families of predictors are available:

(a) a single global model $f_{\theta}:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}$ trained to minimize $\sum_{i=1}^{N} w_i\,\mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal{D}_i}[\ell_i(f_\theta(x),y)]$ for some weights $w_i>0$;

(b) $N$ independent local models $f_{\theta_i}$, each trained only on data drawn from $\mathcal{D}_i$;

(c) personalized models obtained by fine-tuning a globally trained $f_\theta$ on each client's local data, or via multi-task / clustered-client schemes that partition the clients into $K$ groups $\{C_1,\dots,C_K\}$ and train one model $f_{\theta^{(k)}}$ per group.

Personalized architectures may additionally take as input user/context feature vectors $u_i\in\mathcal{U}$, yielding predictors of the form $f_\theta(x,u_i)$.

Address the following three questions:

1. Architectural incorporation of personalization. Specify principled ways of designing the model family $\{f_\theta(x,u)\}$ so that user and context features $u_i$ are exploited to provide personalization while still permitting federated training (i.e., aggregation across clients of the shared parameters of $f_\theta$).

2. Choice of grouping in multi-task / clustered FL. Given the client distributions $\{\mathcal{D}_i\}_{i=1}^N$ (or empirical samples therefrom), give an algorithm and analysis that selects the number of models $K$ and the assignment $\pi:\{1,\dots,N\}\to\{1,\dots,K\}$ minimizing the expected personalized risk $\sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal{D}_i}[\ell_i(f_{\theta^{(\pi(i))}}(x),y)]$, with guarantees relating optimal $(K,\pi)$ to a measure of inter-client distributional similarity.

3. Global vs. local vs. fine-tuned comparison. Identify quantitative conditions on the heterogeneity of $\{\mathcal{D}_i\}$, the per-client sample sizes $n_i$, the hypothesis-class complexity, and any structural assumptions (e.g., shared representations) under which the single global model (a) attains strictly lower expected risk on each client than the corresponding independent local model (b) and than the personalized fine-tuned model (c), and conversely under which (b) or (c) dominate (a).
artifact.status_search_result: The questions remain active research topics. Recent works (2024–2025) propose hybrid and mixture-of-models approaches (e.g., Fed-POE) showing that ensemble/hybrid strategies can simultaneously attain global and personalized regret guarantees, and empirical studies report that local fine-tuning can destabilize globally learned features ("federated feature distortion"). However, no general theory characterizes when the global model dominates independent local or fine-tuned models, nor a definitive algorithm for choosing the number and grouping of models in clustered/multi-task FL. The problem is therefore best classified as open with partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Personalized Federated Learning with Mixture of Models for Adaptive Prediction and Model Fine-Tuning
status_evidence.snippet: The ensemble model can attain the global regret guarantee provided by the federated model... achieving the personalized regret guarantee.
status_evidence.claim: Recent hybrid approaches give partial answers to global-vs-personalized trade-offs.

status_evidence.title: A Closer Look at Personalized Fine-Tuning in Heterogeneous Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Personalized fine-tuning often overfits to skewed client distributions or fails under domain shifts.
status_evidence.claim: When local fine-tuning beats or loses to global models is not yet fully characterized.

status_evidence.title: Personalized Federated Fine-Tuning for LLMs via Data-Driven Heterogeneous Model Architectures
status_evidence.snippet: Heterogeneous personalized architectures continue to be designed for FL.
status_evidence.claim: Architectural design for incorporating user/context features remains an active research direction.
